title: Difference Between Multithreading vs Multiprocessing in Python - GeeksforGeeks
snippet: Due to Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, so multithreading gives concurrency but not parallelism for CPU-bound work. Each process has its own GIL, avoiding this limitation.

title: Multithreading VS Multiprocessing in Python - Contentsquare Engineering
snippet: Threading is best for I/O-bound work (network, disk) since threads can run concurrently while waiting on I/O; multiprocessing is best for CPU-bound work since each process gets its own interpreter and core.
